subtype: Approach: rigid plan that ignores change [Pitfall]
passage: My name is Vikas, and for years a page was taped above my desk: junior accountant, senior accountant, audit manager, each with a date. When Alka told me a team was forming around reporting tools and asked if I'd join, I said no at once. It wasn't on my page. I told myself the page was the whole point. Two years on, the audit posts I was aiming for are fewer, and the openings I read now list skills I never picked up. Alka's team has doubled in size. I still have the page, but I look at it differently. Last week I finally asked Alka what the team has been learning.

qa.q: What was taped above Vikas's desk?
qa.a: A page with a career path on it: junior accountant, senior accountant and audit manager, each with a date.

qa.q: What was Vikas thinking when turning down the offer so fast?
qa.a: Vikas believed the page was the whole point, so anything off it felt like a threat and was refused at once, a rigid and wary stance.

qa.q: What alternative approach could have helped Vikas, and why?
qa.a: Vikas could have tried a short trial with the new team while keeping the page, because a look at the market would have shown the audit path was shrinking.

qa.q: How might Alka have felt hearing that quick no?
qa.a: Alka may have felt disappointed or puzzled, having offered a place and then watched the team double without Vikas.

grounding: Shows a person holding a fixed career plan, refusing a new opportunity in a growing area, and finding the planned path has fewer openings.
